description: Normative v8 directives for the CodeScope review CLI, review profiles, and supplied-evidence boundaries.

authoritativeFor: CodeScope CLI behavior, review and suggestion profiles, and supplied-evidence conventions.
notAuthoritativeFor: Eliware repository requirements, operational procedures, publication, deployment, or Test8 harness behavior.

crosslinks.authoritativeFor: Repository requirements consumed as supplied evidence.
CLI repository requirements consumed as supplied evidence.

dos: Provide a structured, read-only CLI for focused codebase reviews, suggestions, and token estimates.
Keep CLI behavior, review profiles, and supplied-evidence conventions explicit in these directives.
donts: Do not define or enforce Eliware repository requirements owned by Conventions.
Do not define Operations procedures, publication or deployment behavior, or Test8 harness behavior.

dos: Treat the current working directory as the review root.
Keep the reviewed repository read-only and write only CodeScope's own completed output.
Use a deterministic workflow: review supplied context, report findings, and leave fixes and validation to repository owners.
donts: Do not modify repositories, apply fixes, create commits, push, release, publish, deploy, or run repository commands.

dos: Support codescope, codescope --help, codescope all, codescope review <profile>, codescope suggest <profile>, supported direct profile shorthand, and codescope prompt <text>.
Support --usage, --dry-run, --effort=none|low|medium|high|xhigh|max, and --model=gpt-5.6-luna|gpt-5.6-terra|gpt-5.6-sol.
Use the normal repository context for custom prompts while disabling review and suggestion tools.
Use --usage to include provider token and calculated cost data, and use --dry-run to estimate input-token cost without running a model review.
donts: Do not require custom prompts to produce a verdict or a stable response schema.

dos: Read OPENAI_API_TOKEN from a nonblank process environment value first, otherwise from ~/.codescope.
Reject unsafe configuration-file permissions where the platform provides that evidence.
Treat missing credentials and provider transport failures as errors.
donts: Do not place credentials, tokens, environment files, or runtime state in the reviewed repository.
Do not claim that redaction or review context handling is a complete secret-removal boundary.

dos: Assemble comprehensive context in this order: package.json; eligible root, docs, and specs JSON excluding package-lock.json; .github and .knit text configuration limited to 200 lines; Markdown; implementation; test files; and a names-only inventory of remaining files with text line/byte counts and binary byte counts.
Include .js, .mjs, .cjs, and .ts implementation files; matching test files; and Markdown files according to the selected profile.
Read Convention JSON only from the adjacent conventions checkout and report it unavailable when it is not supplied.
Exclude generated coverage directories, dependency directories, Git metadata, and coverage data while retaining legitimate source directories named coverage.
Skip symbolic links and never follow their targets.
Treat excluded or unsupplied evidence as unknown rather than inventing facts.
donts: Do not include package-lock.json as JSON context or include conventions package metadata and lockfiles.
Do not treat files excluded by a profile, absent files, symbolic-link targets, or unsupplied systems as reviewed evidence.

dos: Never run tests in the reviewed repository and never include test execution output in provider context.

Require the AI to perform an independent secret-exposure review over supplied context and report visible or redacted credentials, tokens, passwords, private keys, or other secrets as P0 with location and rotation or revocation guidance.
Treat deterministic redaction and AI detection as incomplete safeguards and keep repository owners responsible for sanitizing supplied material.
donts: Do not claim that CodeScope is a sanitized-environment mode or a complete secret scanner.
Do not rely on CodeScope to make secret-bearing repository or test output safe.

dos: Keep review profiles focused on actionable issues in their declared areas.
Keep suggestion profiles focused on recommendations and exclude them from blocking-verdict policy.
Use the all operation for a comprehensive review of implementation, tests, documentation, package metadata, and the remaining-file inventory, producing one unified review result.
Keep the conventions profile focused on supplied repository documentation, package metadata, specifications, environment documentation, and cross-artifact consistency.
Treat missing or unsupplied artifacts as unknown rather than defects.
Use P0 for immediate emergencies or supplied failing-test evidence, P1 for concrete high-priority defects, P2 for actionable non-blocking issues, and P3 for polish or low-risk follow-up.
Request a provider block verdict for unresolved P0/P1 findings while treating that verdict as provider output only.
donts: Do not make the provider verdict or any finding priority change the CLI exit code.
Do not replace deterministic repository, structural, test, or publication checks owned by other tooling.
Do not repeat issues already documented as known unless implementation contradicts the documented boundary or concrete evidence shows impact outside it.

dos: Write the exact successful provider response unchanged.
Keep provider tool schemas and prompt instructions as requested-output guidance rather than CodeScope acceptance requirements.
Allow review, suggestion, and custom-prompt responses to be provider-defined and not machine-readable.
Report provider transport failures and output-write failures as errors, preserving fallback error metadata where available.
donts: Do not parse, validate, redact, pretty-print, reformat, or otherwise transform successful provider output.
Do not expose or promise a stable CodeScope response schema.
Do not interpret JSON requested from the model or derive process status from provider content.

dos: Keep CI, deployment, registry, Git, rollback, npm pack, npm audit, and other external command state outside CodeScope conclusions unless direct evidence is supplied.
Keep provider internals, operating-system behavior, and delegated child-process mechanics outside the review contract when covered by internal tests.
Keep new feature proposals, repository changes, automatic fixes, commits, pushes, releases, publication, and deployment outside the review operation.
Keep the public README, package metadata, source, tests, and release notes synchronized when changing documented CodeScope behavior.
donts: Do not infer health or alignment for excluded systems from missing evidence.
Do not present CodeScope-local guidance as authority for repository requirements, Operations procedures, publication, deployment, or Test8 behavior.
